sections.heading: £3.99 buys the write-off answer, £9.99 buys the finance answer
sections.html:
Three paid tiers sit above the free one, and the split between them is cleaner than most providers manage. A Basic Check covers police stolen markers, a VIN-to-registration match and mileage data. The Silver Check at £3.99 adds insurance-sourced stolen data on top of the police feed, write-off status, and scrap, unscrapped and salvage history. The Gold Check at £9.99 is the one with the outstanding finance search, a valuation, and what the company describes as "over 80 data points".

The finance result is more detailed than the yes-or-no that some cheap checks return. Where an agreement is live, Total Car Check says the report "will provide details of the agreement type, start and end date and number, as well as the finance provider and finance provider's contact details". That is enough to ring the lender yourself and ask for a settlement figure, which is the only thing that actually resolves the situation. A report that says "finance found" and nothing else leaves you no further forward.

Buying in bulk changes the arithmetic sharply. Gold falls to £4.99 each in a three-pack at £14.99, and to £3.99 each in a five-pack at £19.99. Silver falls to £1.99 each in a five-pack at £9.99. If you are working through a shortlist of four or five cars — which is what most people buying privately actually do — the five-pack is the sensible purchase and the per-report cost lands well under half the single price.

sections.heading: The finance search is Experian's, not the register everyone else licenses
sections.html:
Most of the British vehicle check market runs on one register, licensed out to brands that put their own badge on the front. Total Car Check does not sit in that arrangement. Its finance guarantee is issued by Experian Ltd, named in both the guarantee wording and the privacy policy, and the terms of service describe the underlying feeds as coming from "the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency, the Police, the Motor Insurers' Bureau and their respective data suppliers".

For a buyer this is mostly a point about coverage rather than quality. Finance agreements are registered by lenders with the credit reference agencies, and different agencies do not hold identical files at identical moments. A lender that files with one register and not another produces a clear report on one site and a hit on another, and neither site is lying. It is the strongest argument for treating any single check as one piece of evidence rather than a verdict — and, at these prices, for running a second check from a different data source on a car you are serious about.

The privacy policy also names the other suppliers behind the service, which is more disclosure than the category usually offers: Braintree and PayPal for payments, Cloudflare for fraud prevention, Microsoft Azure for hosting, SendGrid for email, and MyCarNeedsA.com for the garage and servicing information. The company's data protection registration is ZA008598.

sections.heading: What Motorway gets out of a £1.99 report
sections.html:
Motorway is not a small buyer. Its own site claims 8,000+ verified dealers, over 1 million people who have used it to sell a car, an average of £1,600 more than a part-exchange offer, and 84% of sellers getting more than market price. At the time of the acquisition its sales had "more than doubling to a value of £1.7 billion" in 2022, with the platform listing over 1,000 cars a day. It charges the seller a success fee calculated on the final sale price, deducted from the payment, with nothing to pay if the car does not sell.

Put the two businesses side by side and the logic of a £1.99 vehicle check is not hard to follow. Somebody typing a registration into a check site is either buying a car or thinking about selling one, and the second group is exactly who Motorway wants. The check does not have to make money on its own.

There is nothing improper in that, and it is a large part of why the price is what it is. It is worth holding in mind for one reason only: if the same site that valued your car also invites you to sell it, that valuation is being produced by a company with a commercial interest in the answer. Take the number as a starting point and test it somewhere unconnected before accepting an offer.

sections.heading: The £30,000 headline comes with a doorstep checklist
sections.html:
The Gold tier's £30,000 guarantee is a finance guarantee, underwritten by Experian, and it pays "up to the market value of the vehicle at the time you make the claim" subject to that ceiling. It runs for 2 years from the date of the finance check. So far so good.

The conditions are where it gets demanding. Before handing over any money you must confirm that the VIN on the report matches the VIN on the car; confirm the seller's full name "and verify this by checking their passport or driving licence"; confirm the seller's address "by checking a utility bill"; and obtain a signed receipt showing the purchase amount and date. All of it has to happen before the purchase, and the vehicle has to be bought inside the United Kingdom.

Asking a stranger on their driveway for a passport and a utility bill is a reasonable thing to do and almost nobody does it. That is the practical gap in this cover: the guarantee is written for a careful buyer, and the buyer most exposed to undisclosed finance is the one who was in a hurry. There are further exclusions worth reading before you rely on it — a false registration mark or VIN voids it, so does paying "an unreasonable purchase price", defined as below 70% of market value, and cash payments above £1,000 or 10% of the price are not protected.

sections.heading: The other guarantee is smaller than its own number suggests
sections.html:
Stolen markers and write-off categories are covered by a separate document, the Total Car Check Guarantee, and its numbers are considerably tighter than the £30,000 on the front of the Gold tier. On a stolen vehicle it pays the lesser of one third of market value, one third of the purchase price, the cost of acquiring good title, or £10,000. On a Category A or B write-off the ceiling drops to £3,000, and on Category S, C, N or D it drops again to £1,500 — still capped at a third of whichever figure is lower.

A third of the purchase price is the operative limit for most people. On a £6,000 car that is £2,000, not £10,000, and on a Category N result it would be £1,500 at best. The wording also states that the guarantee is limited to VS&TD and police stolen data and does not extend to condition, MOT history or finance, so the two guarantees do genuinely different jobs and neither backs up the other.

The timing conditions are stricter too. The check must have been run "no more than seven (7) days prior to purchasing", and cover lasts 12 calendar months from the order date or until you sell the car, whichever comes first — half the life of the Experian finance guarantee. Free checks are excluded entirely. So are non-UK registered vehicles, salvage auction purchases, cars bought 30% or more below market value, and cash payments above £1,000 or 20% of the price. You must be at least 17, buying privately, at the seller's home address, with a complete V5 whose VIN matches.

sections.heading: Small print that has drifted out of date
sections.html:
Two documents on the site disagree about where the company is. The terms and conditions of service give the registered office as "International House, 24 Holborn Viaduct, London, England, EC1A 2BN". Companies House and the site's own privacy policy both give 12-13 Wells Mews, London W1T 3HE, an address the company moved to on 7 April 2025 from a PO Box in Cardiff. Nothing turns on it for a buyer, but the terms are the document you would quote in a dispute and they are the one that has not been updated.

The cancellation position is stated properly, at least. Total Car Check cites the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 and explains that a single report "is delivered to you, and therefore completed, immediately after you have submitted your request", so the usual 14-day right does not survive delivery. Multi-check packages do keep a 14-day right from the conclusion of the contract, which is a meaningful distinction and one many sites leave vague.

Liability is capped hard. The terms limit "TCC's total aggregate liability" to 125% of the fees paid — on a £9.99 report that is £12.49, outside the guarantees. The accuracy wording is candid about what that means: "Whilst we use reasonable care to ensure data contained within a report is accurate, correct and up to date, TCC cannot guarantee this to be the case."

Support is email only, at enquiries@totalcarcheck.co.uk, "Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm", with a target of replying "within 24hrs". There is no published telephone number and no complaints procedure on the customer support page. For a £9.99 purchase that is defensible; for a £30,000 guarantee claim it means the first step is an email into a queue.

sections.heading: Two marketing claims that do not quite line up
sections.html:
The home page carries "Over 15 years of experience in vehicle history and data" and, a little further down, "Over 300 million checks completed since 2018". The first is right — the company was incorporated in 2009, which is closer to 16 years. The second counts from 2018, and neither figure is dated on the page, so a reader cannot tell whether the 300 million and the "33 million vehicles in the last year" are being measured the same way or which one is current.

The headline price has the same shape. The site's own page title advertises "the lowest cost car check in the UK - £1.99". That price exists, but it is the unit cost of a five-pack of Silver checks at £9.99, and Silver does not include the outstanding finance search. A single check at the advertised tier is £3.99, and a single report with the finance answer in it is £9.99. The £1.99 is real; it is just five checks away, and it is not the product most people arriving from a search for a car check think they are buying.

Neither point is a reason to avoid the service. Both are a reason to read the price table rather than the banner.

sections.heading: Nobody rates vehicle data checks, and nobody arbitrates them
sections.html:
A provenance check is a data service, not a financial one, so the machinery consumers are used to leaning on does not reach it. There is no Financial Conduct Authority permission to look up, no Financial Ombudsman Service to escalate to, and no Defaqto, Which? or Fairer Finance star rating for the category — searching for one returns nothing because none exists. If Total Car Check declines a guarantee claim, the options are its own complaints handling, a chargeback through your card issuer, or the small claims track. That is true of every provider in this market, which is why the wording of the two guarantees above is worth more attention than the headline number on either.

For scale, the Office for National Statistics recorded 312,250 police-recorded vehicle offences in England and Wales in the year ending March 2026, published on 23 July 2026 — down 11% on the previous year, within 1.6 million recorded thefts overall, themselves down 8%. Vehicle crime is falling, and the stolen marker is the least likely of the paid answers to change a purchase. The finance search is the one that earns the £9.99, and it is the one the free tier deliberately withholds.

pros: A genuinely useful free tier — 20+ fields including full MOT history, road tax status and running costs, with no payment and no account
£9.99 for a full check with outstanding finance and a valuation undercuts the established brands by a wide margin
Bulk pricing is aggressive: Gold at £3.99 each in a five-pack, Silver at £1.99 each
The finance result names the lender, the agreement type, the start and end dates and the lender's contact details, so you can get a settlement figure yourself
Finance data comes from Experian rather than the register most rivals license, which makes it a genuine second opinion
The site states plainly what the free check leaves out instead of hiding it behind a quote form
Long-running app with a 4.9 rating from 37,000 App Store ratings and active development since April 2015
Clear, correct treatment of cancellation rights, including the 14-day right that survives on multi-check packages
cons: The £30,000 finance guarantee requires you to check the seller's passport or driving licence and a utility bill, and take a signed receipt, before paying — conditions almost no private buyer completes on a driveway
The separate stolen and write-off guarantee caps at one third of the purchase price, and at £3,000 for Category A/B and £1,500 for Category S/N, so its £10,000 headline is rarely the amount in play
That second guarantee lasts only 12 months and requires the check to have been run within 7 days of purchase, against 2 years on the Experian finance guarantee
The advertised £1.99 is the unit price of a five-pack of Silver checks, and Silver does not include the outstanding finance search at all
The terms and conditions of service still give a Holborn Viaduct registered office; Companies House and the privacy policy give Wells Mews, moved to on 7 April 2025
Total liability outside the guarantees is capped at 125% of fees paid — £12.49 on a £9.99 report
No telephone number and no published complaints procedure; support is email only, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm
The home page claims over 15 years of experience and 300 million checks since 2018 without dating either figure
The company has been owned by the used-car marketplace Motorway since July 2023, and none of the consumer pages say so — the privacy policy refers only to "the Total Car Check group"
No ombudsman, ADR scheme or independent ratings body covers vehicle data checks, so a refused claim ends up at your card issuer or the small claims court
verdict: Total Car Check is the cheapest credible way to answer the two questions that matter about a used car, and the free tier is worth running on any registration before you even arrange a viewing. At £9.99 — or £3.99 each in a five-pack — the Gold report costs little enough that checking three or four cars is a rounding error against the price of any of them, and the Experian-sourced finance data makes it a useful second opinion alongside the register most of the market licenses. Read both guarantee documents before you rely on either: the £30,000 is a finance guarantee with a doorstep checklist attached, and the stolen and write-off cover behind it is measured in thousands rather than tens of thousands. Treat the report as evidence, not as insurance, and it is very good value.

faqs.q: What does the free Total Car Check actually show?
faqs.a: More than 20 data fields at no cost: make, model, fuel type, BHP, road tax status and estimated cost, MPG and running-cost estimates, and the full MOT history. It does not show outstanding finance or insurance write-off status — the company says so explicitly. Those two answers are in the £3.99 Silver check (write-off) and the £9.99 Gold check (finance and write-off).

faqs.q: How much is a full check and is it cheaper in bulk?
faqs.a: A single Gold Check is £9.99. Three cost £14.99, which is £4.99 each, and five cost £19.99, which is £3.99 each. Silver is £3.99 singly and £9.99 for five, or £1.99 each. If you are looking at more than two cars, the multipacks are the obvious buy — and multipacks keep a 14-day cancellation right that a single report loses on delivery.

faqs.q: Is the £30,000 guarantee worth anything in practice?
faqs.a: It is real and it is underwritten by Experian Ltd for 2 years, but it only covers outstanding finance and it attaches conditions most buyers do not meet: verifying the seller's identity against a passport or driving licence, their address against a utility bill, matching the VIN, and taking a signed receipt — all before you pay. Cash above £1,000 or 10% of the price is unprotected, and paying below 70% of market value voids it.

faqs.q: Who owns Total Car Check?
faqs.a: Motorway Online Ltd, which acquired the business on 17 July 2023 and holds 75% or more of the shares and voting rights. Total Car Check Ltd remains a separate company, number 07043189, incorporated on 15 October 2009 and registered at 12-13 Wells Mews, London W1T 3HE. Founder David James joined Motorway as director of vehicle data.

faqs.q: Should I use Total Car Check instead of a check from a different provider?
faqs.a: Use it as well, rather than instead, on a car you are serious about. Finance agreements are registered by lenders with credit reference agencies, and no single register holds every agreement at every moment. Total Car Check's finance data comes from Experian while much of the market licenses one other register, so at £9.99 a second opinion from a different source is cheap cover on a purchase worth thousands.

title: Towergate Boat Insurance
meta_title: Towergate Boat Insurance Review: £5m Cover, New Name
meta_description: Towergate's marine book is now Navigators & General — a 1921 specialist with £5m liability as standard. What moved, what stayed, and what the wording pays.
intro:
Ask for Towergate boat insurance today and you will be dealing with Navigators & General, a Brighton marine specialist that has been writing pleasure craft since 1921. That is not a rebadged call centre: the desk has been quoting yachts, narrowboats, sports boats and dinghies for a hundred and five years, spent forty-one of them inside Zurich after a 1983 acquisition, and moved to The Ardonagh Group in 2024. Most of the staff sail, row or cruise something themselves, which shows in the range — twelve separate products covering everything from a canoe to a commercial workboat.

The standard cover is strong for the money. Third party liability runs to £5 million on yachts, motorboats, sailing craft and small craft, and £3 million of third party and passenger liability on inland waterways. Rescue and evacuation is covered to £50,000, and there is another £50,000 for family and guests hit by an uninsured vessel. Machinery damage is included from new as standard where you can show routine maintenance, tenders stay covered even when used on their own, and an RYA qualification can take up to 10% off the price. Park in a marina and the excess disappears; prove the other party was at fault and it disappears again.

Two things changed underneath the brand and neither was announced loudly. The risk stopped sitting with Zurich on 1 December 2024, and from 1 November 2025 every Towergate marine policy moved to Geo Underwriting Services Limited, trading as Navigators & General. The Towergate name itself was retired across the group on 17 November 2025 in favour of Everywhen. The same team answers the phone on 01242 531172, the cover is largely the same cover, but the names on your certificate are not the names you bought from — and that matters more than it sounds when you come to claim.

sections.heading: Three names between you and the money
sections.html:
Follow the chain and it runs four deep. You buy from Navigators & General, which is a trading name of Geo Underwriting Services Limited, authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 308400 and registered at 2 Minster Court, Mincing Lane, London EC3R 7PD. Geo is the managing general agent — it prices the risk, issues the documents and handles the claim, but the money behind the policy belongs to HCC International Insurance Company plc, trading as Tokio Marine HCC, which holds firm reference 202655 and is regulated by both the FCA and the Prudential Regulation Authority. If you take the optional legal expenses cover, that section is arranged by Arc Legal Assistance and underwritten by AmTrust Specialty Limited under firm reference 202189, so a legal claim goes somewhere different again.

The Towergate side has moved too. Towergate branded policies sat with Advisory Insurance Brokers Limited, firm reference 313250, company number 4043759, which now trades as Everywhen after the group retired the Towergate name on 17 November 2025. The rebrand covered more than thirty-five broking businesses carrying roughly £2 billion of gross written premium and over 500,000 customers across more than 100 UK offices. Type the old Towergate boat address into a browser and you land on an Everywhen page whose only real function is a button reading "Go to Navigators & General". Existing Towergate marine policies keep their old branding until renewal and then come out the other side as Navigators & General documents.

None of that changes your protection. Both firms are FCA regulated, the policy carries Financial Services Compensation Scheme cover, and eligible complaints reach the Financial Ombudsman Service after eight weeks or a final response, whichever comes first. It does change who you ring, and it means a policy schedule from 2023 and a policy schedule from 2026 will name different companies for the same boat.

sections.heading: Agreed value is less agreed than it sounds
sections.html:
Marine insurance is usually sold on the promise that you fix the boat's worth in advance rather than argue about depreciation after a sinking. Navigators & General offers agreed value across its pleasure craft range, and it is worth having. Read the Freedom Sailing wording, though, and the default basis is market value — the cost of replacing the vessel with allowance for type, age and wear — with agreed value sitting as an option in Part B of the policy. Whether you actually bought it will be printed on your schedule and nowhere else, so that line is worth finding before you need it.

Even with agreed value selected, the deduction does not go away entirely. The wording states that deductions for age are made on any life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers at 10% a year up to a maximum of 50%. A five-year-old outboard on an agreed-value policy is therefore a half-price outboard. The same logic runs through the general settlement clause: old materials are replaced with new without a betterment cut, except for sails, protective covers, running rigging, outboard motors, batteries and personal belongings, where the insurer may reduce the claim for age and condition. Those are precisely the items most likely to be damaged.

Personal belongings carry their own ceilings — £300 for any single item, rising to £750 if the boat is your home — and cover for contents stops if the vessel is left unoccupied for more than 45 days in a row. Theft of a tender doubles your excess unless the tender carries a permanent unique identifier. There are useful small benefits pulling the other way: key cover pays up to £500 a claim and £2,000 a year with no excess, and a lockout pays £60 an incident.

sections.heading: The line on your schedule that decides a claim
sections.html:
Cruising limits do more work in marine insurance than any other clause, and this policy runs five of them. Non-tidal UK waters covers inland systems only, with tidal stretches permitted purely to get in and out. Coastal UK waters reaches 12 nautical miles offshore. The continental Brest to Elbe range adds the near continent but forbids anything north of 61 degrees. Elbe to La Rochelle moves its southern boundary with the calendar — 48 degrees north between October and March, 46 degrees north from April to September. The European inland and coastal option holds you to 5 miles offshore. Weather, danger or an order from a government or legal authority are the only permitted reasons to cross the line.

Inland waterways policies work differently again. They are British inland waters only, with no continental extension, but they include up to 30 days of UK coastal use in a policy year at no extra charge, and free personal accident cover to £60,000 for one event covering the owner and non-paying guests. Liveaboard cover extends household belongings, alternative accommodation and £3 million of liability to members of the household.

Some restrictions sit outside the geography. The third party product declines vessels built before 1960, anything capable of more than 50 knots, ferro cement hulls, static houseboats and amateur-built or converted craft. Surveys are generally required on boats over 23 feet and more than 20 years old, and once one is done satisfactorily no further survey is asked for at least five years. Machinery breakdown cover attaches to newer hulls, and here the marketing and the wording do not quite line up: the product pages say cover runs for up to three years from new as standard, while the Freedom Sailing wording conditions that section on the vessel being under five years old from completion of build.

sections.heading: Where the small print will catch you out
sections.html:
Sail alone and read this twice. You are not covered single handed for more than 18 hours in any 24 hour period, and not covered single handed at all if the vessel is over 10 metres, unless the schedule is endorsed to say otherwise. Racing is excluded for masts, spars, fittings, sails and rigging unless Racing Risks has been bought in Part B, though the underwriter will look at events, racing weeks and RORC or JOG entries on referral.

The exclusions read like a surveyor's report. Osmosis, marine growth and gradual water ingress are out. So is gradual deterioration, unless it could not have been spotted by routine inspection or prevented by servicing and maintenance in line with an engineer's, surveyor's or manufacturer's advice — a clause that puts your maintenance record on trial. Machinery failure caused solely by the breakdown of a component part is excluded. Personal accident cover stops entirely at age 75, and medical expenses under the sailing wording pay £500 for any one incident, where the motorboat product page advertises up to £1,000 following an accident on board.

Excess figures are the real gap. Nothing published names a number: the wording refers you to the schedule throughout, so the excess only becomes visible once you have a quote in hand. There is no retail fee schedule on the site either, so instalment charges, mid-term adjustment fees and cancellation costs are not knowable before you engage. A total loss carries no excess, marina and ashore claims carry none, and a proven non-fault claim carries none, which is genuinely good — but the number that applies the rest of the time is yours to extract on the phone.

sections.heading: How to check them, and what nobody publishes
sections.html:
The Financial Ombudsman Service published its 2025/26 annual data on 21 May 2026, recording 214,600 new complaints across all financial products and an average uphold rate of 30%. Pleasure craft is not one of the product lines it breaks out, so there is no boat insurance uphold rate to hold this insurer against — a limitation worth knowing rather than a criticism of the firm. The 14 day cooling-off period applies from the day the documents arrive, and gives a full premium refund provided you have not claimed and do not intend to. Watch the automatic renewal clause if you pay by credit agreement, because consenting to the credit consents to the roll-over.

Two claims made about this insurer could not be verified from outside a quote. No current Defaqto star rating for the pleasure craft range could be found on the provider's own material, so treat any starred badge you see elsewhere as needing confirmation. A multi-vessel or fleet discount is widely assumed to exist for owners with more than one boat, but nothing on the provider's public pages or in the broker product brochure sets out the terms, so ask for it in writing rather than expecting it. Twelve month laid-up policies at reduced rates are confirmed for boats out of use, and small craft moorings allow up to 28 days between April and September.

Before buying, get three things in writing: the excess that applies to a hull damage claim, whether agreed value or market value is showing on your schedule, and the exact cruising range against where you actually intend to go. Then quote it against Craftinsure, GJW Direct and Haven Knox-Johnston, because the pleasure craft market is small enough that the same hull can attract very different numbers.

pros: A genuine marine specialist since 1921, with 105 years of pleasure craft underwriting behind the quote
£5 million third party liability as standard on yacht, motorboat, sailing and small craft policies
No excess at all on a total loss, on claims in a marina berth or ashore, or on a proven non-fault claim
£50,000 rescue and evacuation and a further £50,000 if an uninsured vessel hits your family or guests
Tenders covered even when used independently of the parent vessel
Twelve product lines covering canoes, paddleboards, rowing boats, RIBs, narrowboats, yachts and commercial craft
Up to 10% off for an RYA qualification
Inland waterways policies include 30 days of UK coastal use a year at no extra charge
Key cover to £500 a claim and £2,000 a year, and £60 for a lockout, both with no excess
FSCS protection and Financial Ombudsman access both confirmed in the wording
cons: Agreed value does not stop age deductions: life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers lose 10% a year to a maximum of 50%, even on an agreed-value policy
Market value is the default settlement basis and agreed value is an optional Part B upgrade, so the headline promise depends on a line on your schedule
No excess figure is published anywhere — the wording defers to the schedule throughout, so you cannot compare the real cost of a claim before quoting
No retail fee schedule is published, leaving instalment, mid-term adjustment and cancellation charges invisible until you engage
Sails, covers, running rigging, outboards and batteries are all exposed to age and condition deductions on any claim
Cover for contents stops if the boat is left unoccupied for more than 45 days in a row
Single handed use is limited to 18 hours in any 24, and barred entirely above 10 metres, without an endorsement
Personal accident cover ends at age 75

Marketing and wording disagree in two places: machinery cover is described as three years from new but conditioned on the boat being under five years old, and medical expenses are advertised up to £1,000 while the sailing wording pays £500 an incident
The underwriter changed on 1 December 2024 and the administrator on 1 November 2025, so a claim on an older policy may involve companies you never bought from
Searching for Towergate boat insurance now lands on an Everywhen signpost page rather than a quote form, adding a hop before you reach the product
No current Defaqto rating for the pleasure craft range could be found on the provider's own material
verdict: A century-old marine specialist wearing a new set of names. The cover itself is competitive — £5 million of liability as standard, £50,000 for rescue and evacuation, no excess in a marina or on a total loss, tenders covered independently and up to 10% off for an RYA ticket — and the 1921 pedigree is real rather than marketing. The changes are administrative: Zurich stepped back from the risk on 1 December 2024, Tokio Marine HCC carries it now under firm reference 202655, and the Towergate marine book moved to Geo Underwriting on 1 November 2025 before the Towergate brand itself was retired that same month. What deserves your attention is not the branding but the wording. Agreed value still depreciates outboards, tenders and life rafts at 10% a year to a 50% floor, no excess figure is published anywhere on the public site, single handed cover stops at 18 hours and at 10 metres, and the cruising range on your certificate is the clause that will decide a claim. Get the excess, the valuation basis and the cruising limits confirmed in writing, then quote it against Craftinsure, GJW Direct and Haven Knox-Johnston before you commit.

faqs.q: Is Towergate boat insurance still available?
faqs.a: Not under that name. The Towergate marine book transferred to Geo Underwriting Services Limited, trading as Navigators & General, on 1 November 2025, and the Towergate brand was retired across the group on 17 November 2025 in favour of Everywhen. Existing policies keep their Towergate branding until renewal, then convert. The team is reachable on 01242 531172.

faqs.q: Who actually underwrites the policy now?
faqs.a: HCC International Insurance Company plc, trading as Tokio Marine HCC, under firm reference 202655. Navigators & General is a trading name of Geo Underwriting Services Limited, firm reference 308400, which acts as the managing general agent. Policies written before 1 December 2024 sat with Zurich instead.

faqs.q: How much third party liability do I get?
faqs.a: £5 million as standard on yacht, motorboat, sailing and small craft policies, and £3 million of third party and passenger liability on inland waterways cover, which extends to household members on a liveaboard extension. Marinas, harbours and recognised mooring areas generally require evidence of third party cover before they will take your lines.

faqs.q: Does agreed value mean I get the full sum insured?
faqs.a: Not on everything. Agreed value fixes the vessel's figure, but the wording still deducts 10% a year, up to a maximum of 50%, from life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers. Sails, protective covers, running rigging, batteries and personal belongings can also be reduced for age and condition. Check whether your schedule shows agreed value or market value, because market value is the default.

faqs.q: Will I need a survey?
faqs.a: Generally yes if the boat is over 23 feet and more than 20 years old. Once a survey has been completed satisfactorily, no further survey is normally requested for at least five years. Machinery cover is aimed at newer hulls, so an older boat should expect hull and liability cover rather than breakdown protection.

faqs.q: How far can I sail on a standard policy?
faqs.a: It depends which of the five cruising ranges is on your schedule. UK coastal reaches 12 nautical miles offshore. Brest to Elbe adds the near continent but bars anything above 61 degrees north. Elbe to La Rochelle runs to 48 degrees north from October to March and 46 degrees north from April to September. European inland and coastal holds you to 5 miles offshore. Inland waterways policies are British inland waters plus 30 days of UK coastal use.

faqs.q: What if I have a complaint?
faqs.a: The internal route aims to resolve within three business days, escalating to the Customer Relations Unit with a response inside eight weeks. After that, or after a final response, eligible customers can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR, on 0800 023 4567. The policy also carries Financial Services Compensation Scheme protection.

Trade liability cover here runs to £10,000,000 on public, product and employers' liability alike, with tools insured from £1,000 to £5,000 per person, a £100 standard excess and a single-item cap of £1,500. Those figures come off the provider's own trade pages, read on 21 September 2026. Work at height is quoted to 15 metres and excavation down to 2 metres, and 27 separate trade products are sold, from bricklayers and gas fitters to tree surgeons and scaffolders.

One thing to know before you click, because it decides which website you end up on: Towergate no longer exists as a brand. sections.heading: Your client writes the limit; the scheme only writes it down
sections.html:
Nothing in law tells a builder how much public liability to buy. The number lands on the certificate because somebody further up the chain asked for it, and the pre-qualification schemes that gate most commercial work are more interesting for what they leave out than for what they demand.

Build UK's Common Assessment Standard question set, version 5, dated 1 July 2025 devotes five questions to cover: Q28 employers' liability, Q29 public liability, Q30 professional indemnity, Q31 product liability and Q32 contractors' all risks. Each asks for the same four things — “Policy number, Limit, Excess, Expiry date” — and insists the company name on the policy matches the legal name given at Q1. Q29 is the only one that is compulsory for everybody; Q28 falls away if you employ nobody, Q30 if you are neither Principal Designer nor Designer, Q31 if you supply no materials. Not one of the five sets a minimum figure.

Constructionline's Gold and Platinum supplier checklist guide of February 2026 goes further into the paperwork and no further into the money. It wants certificates, the insurer and the broker, the policy number — “we are unable to accept ‘TBC’ or anything else in place of a Policy Number” — the limit of indemnity, the limit for a single event, the excess, the expiry date, and the broker's business name and telephone number. Again there is no minimum. Design work categories trigger professional indemnity; directly employed staff trigger employers' liability; material supply triggers product liability. The schemes are auditing that you told the truth, not that you bought enough.

That is why the quoted ladder matters more than the ceiling. Cover is sold in £1m, £2m, £3m, £5m and £10m steps with higher limits “on request”, and the step you choose should be read off the contract you are bidding for, not off a brochure. A local authority framework and a domestic kitchen refit do not want the same number, and buying the £10m because it is there is as much of a mistake as buying the £1m because it is cheapest.

sections.heading: A trade policy asks more of you than your van policy does
sections.html:
This is the part most tradespeople have never been told, and it is worth more than any cover limit on the page. A sole trader's own car insurance is a consumer contract. The liability policy he buys the same afternoon is not, and the two sit under different statutes with different consequences for getting a question wrong.

A business policy falls under the Insurance Act 2015, which came into force eighteen months after Royal Assent, on 12 August 2016. Section 3 replaces the consumer's simple duty to answer carefully with a duty of fair presentation: before the contract is entered into, the insured must disclose “every material circumstance which the insured knows or ought to know”, or at minimum give “the insurer sufficient information to put a prudent insurer on notice” that it should ask more. It must be done “in a manner which would be reasonably clear and accessible to a prudent insurer”. In plain terms: the questions on the form are the floor, not the ceiling.

Schedule 1 sets out what happens when that duty is breached. Where the breach was deliberate or reckless the insurer may “avoid the contract and refuse all claims” and “need not return any of the premiums paid”. Where it was neither, the outcome depends on what the insurer would have done knowing the truth: if it would not have written the risk at all it may avoid and refuse claims but must hand the premium back; if it would have written it on different terms, the policy is read as though those terms had always applied. And if it would simply have charged more, paragraph 6 applies the arithmetic nobody expects — the insurer “need pay on the claim only X% of what it would otherwise have been under an obligation to pay”, X being the premium actually charged as a percentage of the premium that should have been. Pay 60% of the right premium and a £50,000 claim settles at £30,000, with the policy still perfectly valid.

Two practical consequences when you take the four-minute quote. Declare the turnover, the trades and the height and depth you actually work to, not the ones you mostly work to. And if there is something the questions never reach — a subcontractor arrangement, an unusual client, a past claim on a different policy — say it anyway, in writing, and keep the email.

sections.heading: Seven insurers, one certificate, and no wording until you ask
sections.html:
Everywhen is a broker, not an underwriter. The trade pages name the paper behind the schemes openly, which is more than many brokers do: AXA, Arch, Covéa, Markel, QBE, Zurich and Intact. That is seven, and every one is an established commercial insurer rather than a start-up MGA. On the contractors' all risks product the page names Markel Direct, a trading name of Markel International Insurance Company Limited, specifically.

What the pages do not tell you is which of the seven you will end up with, or on whose wording. There is no policy document, no insurance product information document and no specimen schedule published anywhere on the trade section; you find out what you have bought after you have given your details and taken a quote. That is normal for a scheme broker and it is still a gap, because the clauses that decide a claim — the tools conditions, the contract works exclusions, the height warranty — live in a document you cannot read in advance.

The product range itself is unusually wide. Twenty-seven separate trade products are sold, covering bathroom fitters, bricklayers, builders, builders' merchants, carpenters, carpet cleaners, construction, contractors, electrical contractors, electricians, engineering, gardeners, gas fitters, groundworkers, handymen, hired-in plant, landscapers, painters and decorators, plasterers, plumbers, professional indemnity, roofers, scaffolders, tools, tradesman, and tree surgeons. Contractors' all risks bundles contract works, hired-in plant, own plant and tools against “fire, flood, storm, malicious damage, and theft”, with legal defence costs from £100,000 and named options for scaffolding, hot roofing, underpinning and hazardous locations — the four things that get a small builder declined elsewhere.

sections.heading: What the van has to be doing at two in the morning
sections.html:
Tools cover is where trade policies are won and lost, and the condition attached to it is stated plainly enough to quote: “Overnight theft is excluded from vehicles unless locked in a secure building.” The van itself has to be “fully secured, all doors and windows closed with all locks fully engaged”, and “where alarms are fitted, they must be set”.

Read that against how most of the trade actually lives. A plumber who parks on the road outside his own house, or in an unlit bay at a travel inn between jobs, has no overnight tools cover at all under that clause — not reduced cover, none. A locked garage, a yard with a shut door, a secure compound: those work. The kerb does not.

The money is worth checking too. The range runs £1,000 to £5,000 per person with a single-article limit of £1,500, which is fine for a bag of hand tools and tight for one modern rotary laser or a decent SDS set. The excess is £100 on each claim. Wear and tear, electrical and mechanical breakdown, damage caused while a tool is in use, and anything “not listed or disclosed” are all outside cover — that last one making the schedule of items you supply at quote stage part of the contract rather than a formality.

sections.heading: The cover that has to outlive the job
sections.html:
Professional indemnity is quoted from £1,000,000 to £10,000,000 and it behaves differently from everything else on the page. Liability cover responds to when the accident happened; professional indemnity responds to when the claim is made. Let the policy lapse and the work you did while insured stops being covered, which is why run-off matters and why the pages raise the point that a claim in tort can arrive well after the six-year contractual limitation period has run out.

Any trade doing design as well as installation needs to take this seriously, because the pre-qualification schemes have already noticed. The Common Assessment Standard waives Q30 only if you are neither Principal Designer nor Designer; Constructionline requires professional indemnity from consultants and from “Contractors with Design work categories”. Specify the boiler as well as fit it, size the steel as well as install it, and you have crossed that line whether or not anyone called it design at the time.

One practical note on the contractors' all risks side: faulty workmanship, wear and tear, design errors, and damage occurring before the policy starts or after the project completes are all excluded. The first and third of those are the gap professional indemnity is meant to fill, so on a design-and-build job the two products are not alternatives — each is the other's hole.

sections.heading: The company that has been through three names
sections.html:
The entity you contract with is Advisory Insurance Brokers Limited, company 04043759, FCA firm reference 313250, registered at 2 Minster Court, Mincing Lane, London EC3R 7PD. Companies House records the history: incorporated on 31 July 2000 as Broomco (2274) Limited, renamed MIA General Insurance Service Managers Limited on 19 September 2000, then Towergate Underwriting Group Limited on 31 December 2003, and finally Advisory Insurance Brokers Limited on 22 March 2022. The Everywhen brand arrived on top of that in 2025; the legal person behind your certificate has not changed since the Towergate years.

Its parent is one of the largest brokers in the world. The Ardonagh Group's full-year 2025 results report pro forma income of $2.9 billion and pro forma adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion, income growth of 20.4%, EBITDA growth of 24.8%, a margin of 35.7% and organic income growth of 4%, across more than 12,000 staff in 250-plus locations in over 30 countries, after 95 acquisitions in the year of which 93 were outside the UK. Chief executive David Ross put it this way: “In the eight years since Ardonagh launched we've seen income grow ten-fold positioning us as a top 15 global insurance broker.”

If something goes wrong, the published timetable is specific. Staff aim to resolve a complaint within three business days; if more investigation is needed you should hear within five business days, again at four weeks with the reason for the delay, and a final response by eight weeks. After that, or if the answer does not satisfy you, the Financial Ombudsman Service at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR will take it — but you must go to them within six months of the final response letter. Policies written at Lloyd's route through Lloyd's own complaints team first.

Note the small-business gate on that last route. The Ombudsman only takes a business complaint where annual turnover is under £6.5 million and either the balance sheet total is under £5 million or there are fewer than 50 employees. Most readers of a tradesman page clear that comfortably; a growing contractor should check before assuming the backstop is there.

pros: Public, product and employers' liability all quoted to £10,000,000, with higher limits available on request
Seven named insurers on the panel — AXA, Arch, Covéa, Markel, QBE, Zurich and Intact — rather than an unnamed one
Twenty-seven separate trade products, including scaffolders, roofers, tree surgeons and groundworkers, which several online-only rivals decline
Work at height quoted to 15 metres and excavation to 2 metres, above the limits many schemes impose
Contractors' all risks bundles contract works, hired-in plant, own plant and tools, with legal defence costs from £100,000 and named options for hot roofing, underpinning and scaffolding
Premiums can be spread over ten monthly direct debits
A clear, published complaints timetable with three-day, five-day, four-week and eight-week stages, and the FCA reference and company number stated openly
cons: No price is published anywhere. Every one of the 27 trade pages gives limits and none gives a premium, so there is no way to benchmark before handing over your details — AXA, Hiscox and Simply Business all publish a starting monthly figure.
No policy wording, insurance product information document or specimen schedule is published for the trade products, so the clauses that decide a claim are unreadable until after you have quoted.
Overnight theft of tools is excluded from vehicles unless the van is locked inside a secure building, which removes cover entirely for any tradesperson who parks on a street or a drive.
The single-article limit of £1,500 inside a £5,000 maximum is low for one modern laser level, plant item or high-end SDS set.
Seven insurers are named but nothing tells you which of them will carry your risk or on whose wording, and the answer changes the claims conditions.

The only terms-of-business document findable on the site is a consumer version dated August 2023; no commercial fee schedule is published, and that document states fees and commission are non-refundable and that refunds under £10 are kept.

The Towergate name is gone from a market that still searches for it, so a tradesman renewing after several years has to satisfy himself the Everywhen site is the same firm before he types anything into it.
verdict: A broad, properly underwritten trade book with seven real insurers behind it and a product list that reaches the awkward trades — scaffolders, roofers, hot-work, underpinning — that the cheap online schemes turn away. The £10,000,000 ceiling on all three liability sections is as high as anyone offers and the 15-metre height and 2-metre depth allowances are genuinely useful. Against that, this is the least transparent of the five tradesman propositions on this site before you quote: no price, no wording, no commercial terms of business. If your work is straightforward and you want a number to compare, start with a provider that publishes one. If your work is the kind that gets declined online, or if you need £5m or £10m because a framework demands it, this is a broker worth the phone call.

faqs.q: Is Towergate tradesman insurance still available?
faqs.a: Yes, under a different name. The Ardonagh Group renamed its advisory arm Everywhen in May 2025 and completed the switch across offices and websites on 17 November 2025, bringing more than 35 broking brands under it. Old towergateinsurance.co.uk trade addresses 302-redirect to the matching everywhen.co.uk page. The regulated company, Advisory Insurance Brokers Limited (FCA reference 313250), is the same one that traded as Towergate Underwriting Group Limited until 22 March 2022.

faqs.q: How much public liability cover do I actually need?
faqs.a: Whatever your client's contract says, because no statute sets a figure. The limits sold here are £1m, £2m, £3m, £5m and £10m, with more on request. Neither of the two schemes that gate most commercial work sets a minimum: Build UK's Common Assessment Standard question set (version 5, 1 July 2025) asks at Q29 only for the policy number, limit, excess and expiry date, and Constructionline's February 2026 Gold and Platinum guide asks for the same plus the broker's name and phone number. Read the limit off the tender document, not off a brochure.

faqs.q: Are my tools covered if they are stolen from the van overnight?
faqs.a: Only if the van was locked inside a secure building. The published condition is that “overnight theft is excluded from vehicles unless locked in a secure building”, and the vehicle must in any case be fully secured with all locks engaged and any alarm set. A locked garage, yard or compound qualifies; a driveway or street does not. Cover runs from £1,000 to £5,000 per person with a £1,500 single-article limit and a £100 excess.

faqs.q: Does the same protection apply as on my own car insurance if I get a question wrong?
faqs.a: No, and this is the most important difference between a business policy and a personal one. A trade policy sits under the Insurance Act 2015, in force since 12 August 2016, which imposes a duty of fair presentation: you must disclose every material circumstance you know or ought to know, not merely answer the questions put to you. Schedule 1 allows an insurer to avoid the contract and keep the premium where a breach was deliberate or reckless, and where it was innocent but a higher premium would have been charged, to pay only the proportion of the claim that your premium bore to the correct one.

faqs.q: Can I take a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service?
faqs.a: Usually yes. You get a final response within eight weeks, and you then have six months from that letter to refer the complaint to the Ombudsman at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR. A business qualifies if annual turnover is under £6.5 million and either the balance sheet total is under £5 million or it has fewer than 50 employees. Policies placed at Lloyd's go through Lloyd's own complaints team first.

title: Trainline Review: The Booking Fee, the Refund Ladder and Who Pays When You Are Late
meta_title: Trainline Review: What the Booking Fee Really Costs
meta_description: Trainline's booking fee runs from 59p to £2.79, and nothing in the app on the day. The refund ladders, the 1 April 2026 rule change and who pays for delays.

headline.label: Booking fee per transaction
headline.value: 59p to £2.79 — nothing at all in the Trainline app on the day of travel

intro:
Trainline charges between 59p and £2.79 to book a British train ticket, and nothing at all if you book in its app on the day you travel. In the year to 28 February 2026 it put £6,319m of tickets through the platform and kept £453m of that as revenue. Both sets of figures are Trainline's own — the fee from its help centre, the money from its results — and were checked on 20 September 2026.

What the fee buys is reach. Trainline's about page describes bringing "the majority of rail and coach operators" in Europe onto one platform, across more than 40 countries, for 27 million active customers of whom 18 million are British. It holds 2.7 million digital railcards, 16% more than a year earlier, and 45% of the digital railcard market among 16 to 30 year olds. Its SplitSave tool, which quietly breaks one journey into several cheaper tickets, saved an average of £13 a trip on bookings between 1 July 2024 and 30 June 2025 by the company's own measurement.

One thing is worth knowing before you book, because it decides who you deal with when a train does not run. Trainline is a retailer, not a railway. The fares belong to the train companies, and so do the tickets, the seat reservations and the compensation. If your train is an hour late the claim goes to the operator that ran it — Trainline will spot the delay and send you a link, but somebody else signs the cheque.

key_facts.value: Trainline.com Limited, company 03846791, incorporated 17 September 1999, at 1 Stonecutter Street, London EC4A 4AH

key_facts.label: Booking fee
key_facts.value: 59p to £2.79 per booking; none in the app on the day of travel; never refundable

key_facts.label: Delivery
key_facts.value: Digital tickets free; station collection £2.99; Royal Mail Special Delivery £12.99; no delivery fees at all through the app

key_facts.label: Refund fee (Trainline's own)
key_facts.value: Nothing under £2, then a ladder rising to £5 a ticket on anything costing £7 or more; £10 to refund a Season Ticket

key_facts.label: Exchange fee (Trainline's own)
key_facts.value: Nothing under £2, rising to £10 a ticket on fares of £15 and above

key_facts.value: £6,319m of net ticket sales and £453m of revenue in the year to 28 February 2026; 27 million active customers
